name: engraphy-desktop
description: Engraphy desktop, a small cross-platform memory console for AI agents. Browse memories, see impact stats, and review the confirm-write queue against your Engraphy MCP server.
author: Engraphy

scripts.build: npm run build:main && npm run copy:renderer
scripts.build:prod: npm run clean && npm run build:main:prod && npm run copy:renderer
scripts.build:test: tsc src/main/client/toolResult.ts src/main/client/webviewMessages.ts src/main/client/statsModel.ts src/main/connection.ts src/main/validation.ts src/main/explorerModel.ts src/main/ipcResult.ts src/main/windowState.ts src/main/messages.ts src/main/graphModel.ts src/main/graphHarvest.ts src/main/versionCheck.ts src/main/updateModel.ts src/main/bootstrap.ts --outDir out-test --module commonjs --target es2022 --skipLibCheck --strict
scripts.test: npm run check-types && npm run build:test && node scripts/test-client.js

comment:deps: The MCP SDK is a BUILD-time dependency: esbuild inlines it into out/main.js and out/stub-server.js, so it is a devDependency and no node_modules ships in the packaged app (electron-builder only bundles production `dependencies`). Pinned to 1.30.0 to match the extension.
comment:graph-deps: cytoscape and cytoscape-fcose are BUILD-time too, for the same reason by a different route: they run in the RENDERER, which is not bundled, so scripts/copy-renderer.js copies their UMD files into out/renderer/vendor and index.html loads them from there. They must be local files -- the renderer CSP is script-src 'self', so a CDN script would be blocked outright.
